text.title: manifest-then-fetch Core Rules
text.summary: Migrated testable rules for manifest-then-fetch. Verify and refine before relying on for production.

rule.statement: Every tool result returned to the model MUST be a JSON object with keys execution_id, preview, size_tokens, and storage_uri. The full body MUST be stored externally and referenced by execution_id.
rule.rationale: Decouples decision-making (small envelope, always in context) from data loading (large body, on-demand). Holds effective context flat across loops, regardless of tool throughput.

rule.statement: The agent MUST call a separate get_full_result(execution_id) tool to load the body. Never inline the body into the manifest.
rule.rationale: Forces an explicit decision before paying the context cost. The model's autonomy stays — it can fetch — but the default is cheap.

rule.statement: Preview MUST be ≤200 tokens AND MUST be structured per tool type: row count + columns for SQL, status + content-type + first 200 chars for HTTP, line count + first/last 5 lines for logs.
rule.rationale: Fixed schema lets the agent parse the preview reliably; a free-text "summary" tempts the model to hallucinate that the body says something it doesn't.

rule.statement: Preview MUST NOT contain the answer the user asked for, even if it fits. If the answer is in the preview, the contract is broken — the tool should have returned a structured answer directly.
rule.rationale: Mixing the answer into the preview short-circuits the protocol: the agent stops fetching but also never learns whether its answer is grounded in the body.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, tool_outputs_avg_bytes is high-tier (at or above 2 KB, the Applies-If line) and store_backend is advanced — an object store with native per-key expiry, i.e. Redis or S3 rather than the local filesystem — the protocol-spec MUST set store_backend to that backend and enforce retention_ttl_seconds through the backend itself (Redis EXPIRE on the body key, an S3 lifecycle expiration rule on the body prefix), not through an application reaper; storage_uri MUST be namespaced per session or tenant (`<backend>://<tenant>/<session>/<execution_id>`) with execution_id a uuid4, and get_full_result MUST refuse an execution_id that belongs to another session. When sensitivity is high the TTL MUST equal its floor, max turn-latency × max_turns (fm-03), and the namespace MUST be deleted at session end; when sensitivity is low the TTL MAY rise to the 24 h ceiling (fm-02). audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Redis documentation (EXPIRE); Amazon S3 documentation (Lifecycle configuration); failure modes fm-02 and fm-03 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A backend that expires keys itself is the only retention guarantee that survives a crashed reaper, and it is what justifies a longer TTL for low-sensitivity bodies. Without per-session namespacing an execution_id is a bearer token for every parked body in the store, and a high-sensitivity payload with a generous TTL sits there long after the turn that produced it.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, tool_outputs_avg_bytes is high-tier (at or above 2 KB, the Applies-If line) and store_backend is not advanced (local filesystem, no native expiry), the protocol-spec MUST list every tool with avg_output_bytes at or above 2 KB in wrapped_tools, set manifest_max_tokens to at most 200 (the r3 cap), choose a structured preview_strategy per tool type as r3 defines, and set retention_ttl_seconds between the floor max turn-latency × max_turns (fm-03) and the 24 h ceiling (fm-02). Because the filesystem does not expire files, the spec MUST name a reaper job and its interval that deletes bodies older than the TTL, and the agent prompt MUST state the fetch condition as `size_tokens > manifest_max_tokens AND the body is needed for the answer` with two worked examples (fm-04). audit.rule_refs cites r1, r2 and r3.

rationale.source: Anthropic engineering, Effective context engineering for AI agents (2025); failure modes fm-02, fm-03 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Above 2 KB per call a single search fills the window inside a handful of turns, so every large tool has to be wrapped, not a sample of them. The filesystem is the one backend in this document with no expiry of its own, which is why the reaper and its interval are part of the spec rather than an operational afterthought; without the stated fetch condition the model fetches everything and the protocol becomes pure overhead.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and tool_outputs_avg_bytes is low-tier — at or above 500 bytes (the Skip-If floor) but under 2 KB (the Applies-If line) — the protocol-spec MUST wrap only the individual tools whose avg_output_bytes in tool-inventory.yaml is at or above 2 KB and return every other tool's result raw; wrapped_tools MAY therefore be a short list but MUST NOT be empty, because an empty list means the skip branch should have fired. store_backend MAY be the local filesystem, preview_strategy MAY be head-N with N at or below 200 tokens, and retention_ttl_seconds MUST be at most 24 h with a reaper (fm-02). Adding Redis or S3, a structured preview or a per-session namespace on this tier requires a rejected-alternatives entry naming the driver that forced it. audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Anthropic engineering, Effective context engineering for AI agents (2025); rules r1-r3 and failure mode fm-02 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A manifest costs roughly the same tokens as a sub-2 KB body, so wrapping a small tool adds a turn and a fetch without saving context; the protocol pays off only on the tools that are actually large. Keeping the store local and the preview simple on this tier keeps the extra fetch step cheap enough that the latency budget in Applies-If still holds.
